got_right: Pre-registered (OSF k2nwj, before the adaptive batches were analysed), with a pure 'Please continue' control and a common covariate-adjusted model for all 32 arms, so the arms are comparable.

Two registered outcomes: affective polarization on the thermometer scale and support for undemocratic practices. This showed that an arm can help on one outcome and not the other (Perception gap video −2.3 on affective polarization, −0.006 on undemocratic practices).
The report hedges honestly: 64 uncorrected tests, two results at p≈0.02 and 0.03, and wide intervals described as inconclusive rather than as null.
Reports the full arm-by-arm tables with n per arm, so the weakly powered arms are visible.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Most arms have 56-330 respondents against a control of 229 (affective polarization) or 234 (undemocratic practices). Standard errors of 1.3-3.3 points mean only effects above about 3-5 points are detectable.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: H1 table: arm SEs 0.997 (Perception gap video, n=641) to 3.251 (dialogue guide, n=65); the 'What makes an American' video estimate of −2.4 had CI [−5.1, 0.4].

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Thirty-two arms were tested on each of two outcomes with no multiplicity correction. The only two hits are near the threshold and would not survive a correction.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Perception gap video p=0.021 and McCain defends Obama video p=0.032, among 64 tests; about 3 false positives are expected at alpha 0.05.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Single-shot exposure with immediate outcomes, and a cross-arm comparison with a shared small control. The batches were adaptive, which complicates comparisons across arms. Durability and behavioural relevance are untested.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Limitations section; arms ranged from 56 to 641 respondents, and the Perception gap video arm was far larger than the others.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Analysis dropped from 6,086 collected to 4,485, and to 3,772 for the affective polarization model. Attrition may differ by arm, and Lucid respondents may be unrepresentative.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: N analysed 4,485 of 6,086; H1 model N=3772; H2 model N=3814.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: The exploratory checks add nothing. The completers-only fit reproduced the planned estimates exactly, and the subgroup interactions were underpowered.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: E1 estimates identical on the same 3,772 respondents; E2 and E3 had 0 of 32 interactions significant, with CIs such as [−14.0, 0.2].

debates.label: Can individual-level interventions move polarization, or is it structural?
debates.position_a: Affective polarization is identity-based, so brief interventions that alter perceptions of the out-group can reduce it, and prejudice-reduction experiments show some average effects.
debates.position_b: Severe polarization is driven by system-level and media dynamics, so brief individual-level messages have little leverage and may even backfire on democratic attitudes.
debates.what_this_study_says: It leans weakly toward the structural side. 30 of 32 arms did nothing detectable on either outcome, and the one affective polarization gain (−2.3) is small and borderline. It cannot rule out modest effects, and it cannot test structural causes directly.

briefs.title: Perception gap video: replication, mechanism and persistence
briefs.question: Does the Perception gap video lower affective polarization by correcting misperceptions of the out-party, and does the effect last beyond the session?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Addresses power and design: it gives the one borderline effect a large pre-registered replication, adds a mechanism measure, and adds a delayed follow-up.
briefs.design_sketch: Arms: Perception gap video, a placebo video of matched length, and a control that just says 'Please continue'. Add a variant of the video without the misperception data to isolate the correction. Measure perceived out-party attitudes before and after exposure (mediator), the affective polarization thermometer, and support for undemocratic practices. Re-contact respondents after about 2 weeks. Lucid-style US sample of Democrats and Republicans, with one primary test.

power_target.basis: Observed −2.3 points with SE 0.997 at n=641; the true effect is probably smaller than the winning estimate, so size for about 1.4 points (SD about 20 implied by the SEs).

briefs.title: Individual message versus structural cue
briefs.question: Does the Perception gap video's effect shrink when respondents are primed with a hostile, elite-driven polarization environment?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Addresses framing: it tests whether individual-level correction is overridden by structural cues, instead of assuming either side.
briefs.design_sketch: A 2x2 factorial: Perception gap video versus control, crossed with a prime (a realistic feed of elite and media hostility versus a neutral feed). Outcomes are affective polarization and support for undemocratic practices. If the video effect holds under the hostile prime, individual-level interventions have leverage. If it vanishes, the structural account is supported.

power_target.basis: Interaction contrast; the observed main effect of −2.3 with SE 1.0 at n=641 implies an interaction needs roughly 800 per cell.

briefs.title: Who does the Perception gap video work for?
briefs.question: Does the video's effect on affective polarization vary by partisanship, political interest and the size of baseline misperception?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Addresses sample and measurement: the exploratory interactions were too noisy (CIs of ±7 points), so a dedicated, powered moderator test is needed.
briefs.design_sketch: Video versus control, with stratified recruitment of Democrats and Republicans, high and low political interest, and a pre-treatment measure of out-party misperception. Pre-register the three interactions. Use a probability-based or quota panel in addition to Lucid.

power_target.basis: E2/E3 interaction SEs of 3-3.6 at the arm sizes used; the interaction MDE needs about 4x the n of the main effect.

verdict: A follow-up is worth running, but only a narrow one. Of 64 tests, two were barely significant and 30 of 32 arms were inconclusive, so the broad screening design should not be repeated. Run the Perception gap video replication with a mechanism measure and a delayed follow-up first, since it is the only affective polarization result and also the largest arm. The McCain defends Obama video effect on undemocratic practices rests on 86 people and is probably noise. The structural-cue and moderator briefs can follow if the replication holds.
